title: Controlled Failover Game Day Plan (2025 Q2)
author: Tomáš Novák
body:
h1. Purpose
This game day validates Redwood Inference’s upgraded automated regional failover workflow in a controlled, safety-guarded way. The intent is to build confidence in:
- Trigger evaluation (signals, windows, hysteresis, hold-down timers)
- Orchestration correctness (progressive failover, rollback)
- Safety checks (“safe-to-failover” gating on capacity and dependency health)
- Operator experience (dashboards, alerts, incident bot messaging, runbook steps)

This is a *controlled test*, not a DR event. We will keep blast radius small, use progressive routing, and keep manual override available at all times.

h1. Date / window
- Target window: 2025-04-29 10:00–12:00 PT (primary)
- Backup window: 2025-05-06 10:00–12:00 PT
- Change freeze exceptions: Approved for the window only. All changes are scoped to feature flags + routing policy changes with defined rollback.

h1. Systems in scope
In-scope (phase 1):
- Hosted API traffic only (Redwood API)
- Routes:
  - /v1/chat.completions (streaming + non-streaming)
  - /v1/embeddings
- Region pair for failover:
  - Primary (degraded): us-east-1
  - Target (failover): us-west-2
- Trigger engine + orchestrator:
  - Health signal aggregator
  - Failover trigger engine (with hysteresis/hold-down)
  - Failover orchestrator state machine
  - Routing policy updates (percentage-based)
  - Incident bot notifications to #incidents

Out of scope (this game day):
- Dedicated capacity customers (Dedicated)
- Redwood Private deployments (VPC/on-prem)
- Cross-cloud or multi-provider routing
- DNS TTL experiments beyond existing conservative defaults (we will not change TTLs during this test)

h1. Hypotheses
H1: Signal aggregation + trigger evaluation detects partial regional impairment within the expected window and transitions to DEGRADED (not FAILED) before progressing.
- Expected: detection within 2–5 minutes depending on scenario.

H2: Progressive failover ramps traffic from us-east-1 to us-west-2 without causing customer-visible hard failures.
- Expected: limited, measurable latency increase during transition; error rate remains within stop conditions.

H3: “Safe-to-failover” checks prevent unsafe action when target region capacity headroom is insufficient or a critical dependency is unhealthy.
- Expected: orchestrator blocks transition and emits a clear audit event + incident bot message.

H4: Rollback is reliable and returns the system to steady state without flapping.
- Expected: rollback completes within 5 minutes; hold-down timers prevent immediate re-trigger.

H5: Operator experience is workable.
- Expected: on-call can answer: (a) what state are we in, (b) why did we transition, (c) what is the next recommended action, (d) how to override/rollback.

h1. Blast radius / customer scope
We will scope traffic using routing policy gates:
- Eligible traffic: internal canaries + “Dev/Free” tier only
- Initial ramp: 1% of eligible traffic, then 10%, then 25% (max) unless explicitly approved by IC
- Explicit exclusions:
  - Any enterprise allowlists
  - Dedicated capacity tenants
  - Customer routes flagged as “no-cross-region”

Definition: “Eligible traffic” is defined by routing policy match rules (customer tier + route + model family + region).

h1. Preconditions (go/no-go)
All items must be GREEN before initiating impairment.

h2. Capacity / fleet readiness
- us-west-2 GPU pool headroom:
  - >= 30% headroom on target pools for the in-scope model families
  - Queue depth < 30s equivalent backlog (per pool)
- Cross-region egress budget acknowledged by Infra

h2. Dependency health
Must be healthy in both regions:
- Auth/token verification
- Routing policy store
- Model artifact registry access
- Telemetry ingestion (allowed to be degraded, but should not page)
- Any required vector/rerank dependencies for selected routes (if used)

h2. Observability readiness
- Dashboards validated and shared in #incidents thread:
  - Region health overview
  - Failover state transitions + audit log
  - Customer impact by tier
  - Capacity headroom (target region)
- Alerts temporarily adjusted for game day (if needed) and documented under “Temporary changes” below

h2. Change management / approvals
- IC + Release Eng sign-off required to enable automation in production (even scoped)
- Manual override permissions confirmed (RBAC)
- Rollback plan reviewed and a “do now” command snippet ready

h1. Roles and responsibilities
h2. Required roles
- Incident Commander (IC): Rafael Mendes
  - Owns go/no-go, step transitions, and stop/rollback decisions
- Operations Driver (hands-on-keyboard): Miles Thornton
  - Executes orchestrator commands, feature flag flips, and routing changes under IC direction
- Observability Lead: Aisha Bello
  - Watches SLO/burn-rate, tail latency, error rates; calls out risk early
- Routing/Platform Observer: Mina Haddad
  - Confirms routing policy changes behave as expected; watches for policy complexity regressions
- Infra/Capacity Observer: Irene Choi
  - Confirms target region capacity posture; approves ramp stages from a fleet perspective
- Comms Lead (internal): Tomáš Novák
  - Maintains #incidents timeline, posts updates, prepares customer-facing comms only if needed
- Release / Change Manager: Connor O'Brien
  - Confirms we’re within approved window and that rollback artifacts are ready

h2. Optional / on-call backup
- DNS/Edge escalation: Victor Alvarez (only if we hit edge routing issues)

h1. Communication plan
h2. Channels
- Primary coordination: #incidents (single thread named “2025Q2 controlled failover game day”) 
- Heads-up: #announcements (short message 30 minutes before)
- Escalations:
  - Infra: #eng-infra
  - Platform/Routing: #eng-platform
  - Support liaison (only if customer impact occurs): #support

h2. Updates cadence
- Every 10 minutes during active phases (impairment + ramp)
- Immediately on any state transition (per orchestrator) and on any stop condition trigger

h2. Status page policy
- No proactive public status page update for the planned test at current blast radius.
- If customer impact exceeds stop conditions or escapes scope, Comms Lead will coordinate with Support to publish a short status note.

h1. Safety controls
- Automation mode: start in MONITOR-ONLY, then ENABLED for eligible traffic only
- Hysteresis + hold-down timers enabled (per ADR)
- Manual override always available (disable automation + pin region)
- Progressive ramp with explicit checkpoints (IC approval required)

h2. Hard stop conditions (abort + rollback)
If any occur, IC calls immediate rollback to steady state and ends the test.
- Target region (us-west-2) elevated failures: 
  - 5xx >= 2.0% for 3 consecutive minutes for in-scope routes, OR
  - Timeouts >= 1.0% for 3 consecutive minutes
- Tail latency regression:
  - p99 latency > 2.0x baseline for 5 consecutive minutes (in-scope routes)
- Capacity risk:
  - Target GPU headroom drops below 15% sustained for 3 minutes, OR
  - Queue backlog > 60 seconds sustained for 3 minutes
- Scope breach:
  - Any enterprise or Dedicated traffic is routed cross-region unintentionally
- Flapping:
  - More than 2 failover state oscillations within 20 minutes
- Operator uncertainty:
  - If we cannot confidently determine current state and next action within 5 minutes (dashboard/telemetry outage), revert to safe steady state

h2. “Soft stop” conditions (pause escalation)
- Any alert paging outside the expected set for the game day
- Elevated customer tickets/complaints observed by Support (even if metrics look okay)

h1. Test scenarios
We will run at most *two* scenarios in the primary window. If scenario 1 is noisy or we hit soft-stop conditions, we do not proceed to scenario 2.

Scenario 1 (preferred): Partial impairment in us-east-1 (increased error + latency)
- Induce: controlled fault injection (service-level) to create elevated 5xx and mild packet loss characteristics for a subset of traffic
- Expected orchestrator behavior:
  - Transition: HEALTHY -> DEGRADED
  - Consider progressive failover only if DEGRADED persists and meets trigger criteria

Scenario 2 (optional): Dependency health gating
- Induce: simulate “unsafe-to-failover” by temporarily lowering capacity headroom signal or marking a dependency unhealthy in us-west-2
- Expected orchestrator behavior:
  - Trigger evaluates impairment but blocks FAILOVER action due to safety gate
  - Emits audit event with explicit reason

h1. Step-by-step run of show
All times relative to T0 (start of test). IC may pause at any point.

h2. Phase 0 — Pre-flight (T-30 to T0)
1) Create #incidents thread with:
   - Dashboard links
   - This runbook section copy/paste
   - Current config snapshot (feature flags + routing policy version)
2) Confirm go/no-go checklist:
   - Capacity headroom in us-west-2
   - Dependency health
   - Alerting set
3) Set automation to MONITOR-ONLY:
   - Confirm orchestrator shows MONITOR-ONLY in audit view
4) Baseline capture (Observability Lead):
   - 15 minutes baseline for error rate and p95/p99 latency per route
   - Baseline for queue depth and GPU utilization

h2. Phase 1 — Enable scoped automation (T0 to T+10)
1) Operations Driver enables automation for *eligible traffic only*:
   - Feature flag: failover_automation_v2 = ON (scoped)
   - Policy guard: eligible_tiers = [internal, dev_free]
   - Max progressive failover cap = 25%
2) Validate no change in routing at steady state:
   - Confirm traffic stays in us-east-1
   - Confirm orchestrator remains HEALTHY

Success criteria:
- No increase in 5xx/timeouts vs baseline
- Audit log shows “enabled (scoped)” event

h2. Phase 2 — Induce impairment (T+10 to T+30)
1) Operations Driver induces impairment in us-east-1 for in-scope routes.
2) Observability Lead monitors:
   - Region health signals: error rate, tail latency, network probes
   - Customer impact panels
3) Confirm trigger evaluation:
   - Trigger engine enters DEGRADED (expected within window)
   - Incident bot posts state + top contributing signals

Success criteria:
- Trigger engine transitions to DEGRADED with correct reasoning
- No flapping; state remains stable under hysteresis rules

Stop conditions:
- If impairment causes errors > thresholds across broader traffic, abort immediately

h2. Phase 3 — Progressive failover ramp (T+30 to T+70)
Only proceed if IC approves.

1) Check “safe-to-failover” gates:
   - us-west-2 headroom >= 30%
   - Dependency health GREEN
   - Routing policy sanity check passes
2) Start progressive routing:
   - Stage A: 1% of eligible traffic -> us-west-2 (hold 10 minutes)
   - Stage B: 10% (hold 10 minutes)
   - Stage C: 25% (hold 10 minutes)
3) At each stage:
   - Validate error + latency within bounds
   - Validate no scope breach (enterprise/Dedicated)
   - Confirm audit log captures stage transition + reason

Success criteria:
- At each ramp stage:
  - 5xx < 2.0% sustained
  - p99 latency does not exceed 2x baseline for >5 minutes
  - Queue depth stable and no capacity alarms
- Operator can correlate transition -> metrics impact -> expected next action

Stop/rollback:
- If any hard stop condition occurs, rollback to Stage 0 (0% routed) immediately

h2. Phase 4 — Rollback + recovery verification (T+70 to T+95)
1) Disable impairment in us-east-1.
2) Rollback progressive routing to 0%.
3) Keep automation ENABLED (scoped) for 10 minutes to validate we do not re-trigger.
4) Return automation to MONITOR-ONLY after verification.

Verification checklist:
- Orchestrator returns to HEALTHY (or DEGRADED briefly then HEALTHY)
- No routing residuals (policy reflects 0% failover)
- Error rates and latency return to baseline bands
- Audit log includes rollback action and operator identity

h2. Phase 5 — Optional Scenario 2 (T+95 to T+115)
Only proceed if Phase 4 completed cleanly and IC approves.

1) Simulate unsafe-to-failover gate (capacity/dependency) in us-west-2.
2) Re-induce mild impairment signal in us-east-1.
3) Confirm orchestrator refuses to progress failover and documents reason.

Success criteria:
- Failover action is blocked with explicit “unsafe-to-failover” reason
- Operators can see the gating signal in dashboards

h1. Success criteria (overall)
The game day is considered successful if:
- We can safely induce impairment and observe correct signal/trigger behavior.
- Progressive failover ramp succeeds at least through Stage B (10%) without breaching stop conditions.
- Rollback restores steady state with no flapping.
- Audit trail is complete: who/what/why for each transition.
- Post-test actions are captured with owners and due dates.

h1. Artifacts to capture during the test
- Timeline in #incidents thread (IC/Comms Lead)
- Screenshots or exported panels:
  - Region health signals
  - Failover state machine transitions
  - Customer impact by tier
  - Capacity headroom
- Config snapshots:
  - Feature flag state
  - Routing policy version/hash
  - Trigger thresholds in effect
- Any anomalies and whether they were expected

h1. Temporary changes (must be reverted)
- Any alert routing overrides or muted alerts must be listed here with revert time.
- Any dashboard annotations used to reduce noise should be documented.

h1. Post-game-day steps
Within 2 business days:
1) Post-test retro doc created (owner: Tomáš Novák)
   - What went well / what was noisy
   - False positives/negatives in triggers
   - Any operator confusion points
2) File follow-ups in Linear under ENG-2841 umbrella:
   - Threshold tuning items (owner: Aisha Bello)
   - Safety gate improvements (owner: Miles Thornton)
   - Routing policy guardrails (owner: Mina Haddad)
3) Update runbook if any steps were unclear:
   - Automated Region Failover Runbook (owner: Tomáš Novák)

h1. Appendix A — Operator commands / quick actions (reference)
Note: exact commands depend on environment; use the runbook for the canonical copy.

- Check current failover state:
  - incident-bot: /failover status us-east-1
- Set MONITOR-ONLY:
  - orchestrator: set-mode --region us-east-1 --mode monitor-only
- Enable scoped automation:
  - orchestrator: set-mode --region us-east-1 --mode enabled --scope dev_free,internal
- Progressive routing stage:
  - orchestrator: set-failover-percent --from us-east-1 --to us-west-2 --percent 10 --scope dev_free,internal
- Emergency rollback:
  - orchestrator: set-failover-percent --from us-east-1 --to us-west-2 --percent 0 --scope all
  - orchestrator: set-mode --region us-east-1 --mode monitor-only

h1. Appendix B — Metrics to watch (minimum set)
- Request error rate (5xx) by region, route, and tier
- Timeout rate by region
- p95/p99 latency by region and route
- Streaming disconnect rate (for streaming chat)
- Queue depth and queue time by region + GPU pool
- GPU utilization + headroom signals
- Trigger engine state + contributing signals
- Orchestrator transition events + audit log integrity
